description:
Link checking honours a document reference's commit pin instead of demanding the file in the working tree.

## Background

A document reference may pin a commit, which records the version the reference names. `jit validate` resolves such a reference against its pin and passes.

`jit doc check-links` does not. It reads the working tree and reports `missing_document` for a pinned reference whose file has since been deleted, so a repository whose references all resolve is reported as having errors.

Measured on this repository: issue `41aa1b75` carries three references pinned to commit `6b799832`, whose files were deleted from the working tree in a later commit. All three resolve at the pin — `git cat-file -e 6b799832:<path>` succeeds for each — and `jit validate` reports zero errors. `jit doc check-links` reports all three as `missing_document` errors and exits 1.

A pin exists precisely so a reference keeps naming a version the working tree has moved past. A checker that ignores it turns every pinned historical reference into a permanent error, and the archival workflow creates pinned references by design.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A document reference pinned to a commit where its file exists is reported as valid, whether or not the file is in the working tree.
- [hard] REQ-02: A pinned reference whose file is absent at its pinned commit is still reported as an error.
- [hard] REQ-03: The two commands agree: whole-repository validation and link checking classify a pinned reference the same way.

## Notes

Surfaced by the archival-layout epic `8e071e18` while reconciling that epic's requirement that every document reference resolves. Three references do not resolve by link checking's reckoning and all three resolve by the validator's; the validator is right. Outside the epic's criteria — its gate is whole-repository validation, which passes.
title: Honour a document reference's commit pin when checking links
